titel: 1873: The year America ditched silver as money and all hell broke loose

einzeiler: How an 1873 US monetary law sparked global economic turmoil and fierce political division.
kurzfassung: In 1873, a seemingly minor U.S. law effectively ended the bimetallic standard and locked the nation into gold, triggering a severe economic depression and decades of populist anger. The resulting deflation crushed heavily indebted farmers and fueled intense political battles, led by figures like William Jennings Bryan. Ultimately, the episode demonstrates the dangerous ripple effects of monetary policy and the recurring allure of precious-metal standards in times of economic stress.
stichpunkte: Passage of the Coinage Act of 1873 quietly eliminated the standard silver dollar, locking the U.S. into a gold standard.
The law restricted liquidity precisely when global financial panics and bank crashes created a desperate need for cash.
Germany's simultaneous shift to gold created a massive silver glut, crashing global silver prices by over 50%.
A protracted six-year recession and a twenty-year deflationary spiral devastated American farmers with fixed mortgage debts.
Senator John Sherman faced severe backlash as the architect of the bill, while critics dubbed the legislation the 'Crime of 1873'.
Populist anger fueled conspiracy theories blaming foreign bankers, echoing long-standing xenophobic and anti-Semitic tropes.
William Jennings Bryan rose to political prominence in the 1890s through his passionate free-silver campaign and iconic Cross of Gold speech.
New South African gold discoveries eventually ended the global gold drought, defusing the silver movement and cementing gold's dominance.

clips.hook: The accidental omission that changed monetary history
clips.text: lawmakers failed to include the traditional silver unit in the new coinage legislation, effectively removing silver from the currency system.

clips.hook: A seventy-year price stability erased in years
clips.text: The market value of silver held steady for decades before plummeting significantly following the legislative change and shifting global policies.

clips.hook: Why reversing the silver ban was impossible
clips.text: Attempting to restore silver at that stage would have triggered an overwhelming influx of foreign sellers draining the nation's gold reserves and forcing a drastic devaluation.

clips.hook: You shall not crucify mankind upon a cross of gold
clips.text: The orator delivered a dramatic warning against sacrificing working people to the rigid demands of the gold standard.

clips.hook: Why monetary policy belongs outside politics
clips.text: Elected officials struggle to resolve economic matters objectively, making independent central banks essential for acting in the broader national interest.

beschreibung:
In 1873, Ohio senator John Sherman quietly helped pass a law that stopped Americans from turning silver into official US money. The consequences were huge: years of economic pain and political turmoil that earned it the nickname “the Crime of 1873”. Pulitzer Prize-winning author Liaquat Ahamed explains how the event squeezed American farmers and fuelled the Free Silver movement, led by the populist firebrand William Jennings Bryan. Host Gillian Tett explores with Ahamed how monetary policy can reshape politics.

Further reading:
1873: The Rothschilds, the First Great Depression, and the Making of the Modern World (2026), by Liaquat Ahamed
